issue.title: The bash() tool call uses sh instead of bash
issue.body:
As part of its task, my vibe called bash:

```
bash(command='cd /home/tyl/llm/index-benchmark && source .venv/bin/activate && python retriever/luxical/index.py dataset/documents > test_luxical_index.jsonl 2>&1 | head -20', timeout=None)
Error: bash failed: Command failed: 'cd /home/tyl/llm/index-benchmark && source .venv/bin/activate && python retriever/luxical/index.py dataset/documents > test_luxical_index.jsonl 2>&1 | head -20'
Return code: 127
Stderr: /bin/sh: 1: source: not found
```

`source`, of course, is [part of bash's built-ins](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/bash.1.html#SHELL_BUILTIN_COMMANDS) to load shell code from a file. Shouldn't the bash tool support it?

Sadly, [vibe's bash tool call runs](https://github.com/mistralai/mistral-vibe/blob/402e898f391f65c447cfe061a5fee47a0b50cce7/vibe/core/tools/builtins/bash.py#L240-L248) `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell()` which [uses](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/4ea3c1a04747978361b497798428423cbb6a7146/Lib/asyncio/unix_events.py#L844-L846) `subprocess.Popen()` [which runs](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/4ea3c1a04747978361b497798428423cbb6a7146/Lib/subprocess.py#L1845-L1851) `/bin/sh`, not bash.

I can certainly understand why my dear devstral model would confuse the bash tool for running bash rather than sh.
Shall we have it run bash?

I believe the trick is to pass `executable="/bin/bash"` as kwargs to `asyncio.create_subprocess_shell()`.

steps: Create a Python virtual environment in the workspace: run `python3 -m venv .venv` with the bash tool, then confirm `.venv/bin/activate` exists.
Activate that virtual environment and print the active interpreter in a single shell command: `source .venv/bin/activate && which python`.
expected: The bash tool should run the command through a shell so the `source` builtin works and the command succeeds (per the issue discussion the tool is expected to execute bash/shell semantics).
defect: The command string is handed to the ACP terminal without a shell, so `source` is treated as a program and the step fails with a 'not found' / 'Failed to create terminal' style error instead of activating the venv.

Root cause: The ACP Bash implementation tokenizes commands with shlex.split and sends an executable plus literal arguments to terminal/create without a shell. A shell builtin such as source therefore becomes an executable lookup and shell operators are not interpreted. This is the path exercised by the archived ACP case. The standalone CLI /bin/sh compatibility issue is a separate path.
